source.commit_role: Baseline for the reviewed definitions; the atlas flags later definition changes. Drawing hashes pin the current catalog and geometry. order_hasse_review and state_overlap_review supersede the mathematical Order and State drawings from order_state_integration, retaining Coordination Order. structured_configuration_correction still supersedes the earlier Configuration alias assessment. process_preservation_review supersedes the Change, Feeds, Causal path, Causal Contribution, Invariant, Persistence and Constraint drawings and assessments. identity_expression_review supersedes the Entity, Environment, Scope, Specification, Rule and Sign drawings and assessments, and records Daniel's retention of Boundary and Representation over tentative study proposals. expression_recording_review supersedes the Language, Map, Record and Observation drawings. action_interior_review supersedes the Model, Action, Consequence, Interpretation, Agency, Tool, Capability, Memory, Exposure, Bodily Organization, Embodied Perspective and Internal Activity Selection drawings and assessments, and records Interior's retention. coordination_review supersedes the Flow, Interface, Control, Standing, Recognition and Principal drawings and assessments, and records the retention of Claim and ActsFor. institutional_review supersedes the CountsAs, Authority, Permission Claim, Declaration and Permission drawings and assessments, records the retention of Admission and Revocation, and leaves Grant unresolved. Earlier dated decisions, the runes.js hash, migration_note and method describe historical review stages, not current counts or an assertion that this follow-up changed no drawings.
source.migration_note: The runes.js hash is historical: it pins the original SVG module as it existed at b8ea7233 (the original review's source commit); that file is no longer in the tree. glyph-catalog.mjs was the shared-source migration of that module with unchanged paths (sha256 60c2bb24…, committed in ae6cce9). This review describes the revised catalog pinned above, including refinements made to revised paths after the previous write of this file; entries were reconciled to those actual paths, which is a factual correction, not a new semantic approval. Clearance remarks use glyph-geometry.json: 32-unit canvas, stroke width 1.1, square caps, miter joins. Exactly 49 glyph paths differ from ae6cce9: the 43 entries previously marked revise plus six linked family members (State, Interface, ConstituentPower, OperativeKnowledge, WarrantedKnowledge, Attention). The other 66 paths are byte-identical; their entries were edited only to remove statements about counterparts' old paths and to record remaining concerns. Codepoints are unchanged. Ontology hashes are unchanged. Cross-catalog collision findings about historical Unicode candidates describe the pre-migration site. Risk wording records possible reader inferences, not entailments established by graphic composition.

method: Editorial review of each custom SVG glyph's actual drawn path in proposals/glyph-catalog.mjs (32-unit grid, rendered at stroke-width 1.1) against the full binding definition of its term. 'trial' means a defensible learned mnemonic to be shown with its label. 'revised' means the author redrew the glyph after the previous review (ae6cce9), either because it was marked revise or as a linked family member; it is a revised trial awaiting design and reader review, not approved and not semantically certified, and the entry records what the new motif addresses and what risk remains. 'revise' (currently assigned to no entry) means a glyph actively imports an entailment the definition denies, collides with an adjacent term, or relies on a cue too weak to distinguish it. Single-path meanings are mnemonics, not formal diagrams: stroke names in the catalog document design intent only, and junctions, enclosures and arrowheads do not assert Causal paths, proofs, entailments or exhaustive depictions. Judgments are not measured scores, reader studies, proofs of semantic equivalence, or claims that any reader innately decodes a glyph. Omitting part of a definition is not by itself grounds for revision. Stroke clearances are computed from path coordinates and the geometry specification, not from rendered or reader tests. This review update changed no glyph shape; it reconciles entry text to the pinned catalog paths.

relation_review.decision: Use two equal horizontal bars joined by a central vertical stroke extending four grid units beyond them. Daniel chose this crossed-equals form after considering a plain and offset H. The connection is a mnemonic for association, not an assertion of Identity or a compositional operation on it.
relation_review.scope: Only Relation's drawing changes; its font slot, definition and all other glyph paths are retained. Interface keeps the previous ordered-path motif. The new mark uses Identity's bar coordinates and the existing grid and stroke rules.
relation_review.open_gate: The double-dagger footnote reading and resemblance to Identity remain risks. Two bars do not limit Relation to two participants; graphic symmetry does not require a symmetric Relation, and the drawing does not specify ordered roles by itself. Retain labels; no reader study establishes recognition or small-size discrimination.

denotation_review.decision: Use a maps-to glyph: a vertical tail bar, horizontal stem and right-facing arrowhead. Daniel approved borrowing the expression-to-target roles of mathematical maps-to notation, without importing a function's uniqueness condition.
denotation_review.scope: Only Denotation's drawing changes. The existing font slot, all other glyph paths and all definitions are retained. The custom drawing follows the integer grid, uniform stroke and axial-angle guides; it does not depend on a system font's maps-to character.
denotation_review.open_gate: Within a function each input has one output, but Denotation only names an expression and its target; it does not require the same expression to denote the same target across uses. The arrow asserts neither causation, fidelity, Truth, Interpretation nor institutional status. Retain labels and test the tail at small sizes; no reader study establishes reliable interpretation.

set_configuration_review.decision: Set is three solid dots in a triangle; Configuration is those same dots joined by straight lines. Set's font slot is appended, while its presentation follows the registry before Configuration. State retains its old drawing pending separate review.
set_configuration_review.boundary: The geometric family is a mnemonic, not a compositional semantics. Neither exactly three members nor complete connectivity is required. Configuration remains the extensional Set construction in relational use, so the drawn edges do not prove a separate kind, participant closure, or mandatory Relation membership. Identifier consolidation remains open. Set may resemble the therefore sign; Configuration may resemble a triangular network or Change's triangle.

order_hasse_review.boundary: Hasse edges show cover relationships, omitting reflexive loops and transitive shortcuts. The example does not require every Order to have three members, a greatest member, branching, finiteness or incomparable members; empty and total Orders remain permitted. Upward reading is a learned convention, not authority, causation or improvement. Omitting Configuration's bottom line is not an ontological subtraction operation.

process_preservation_review.scope: Only these seven drawings change, retaining U+E00B through U+E011, every other glyph path and slot, and all ontology definitions. Node drawings follow the existing stroke-only font conventions: hollow r=2 rings, solid concentric disks, and connections stopped 2.5 units from node centers, so hollow centers stay transparent without opaque masks. process_preservation_review.boundary: The new motifs are term-specific mnemonics or candidate cues: part-to-part bridge, comparison lanes, open pivot fan and stop-versus-passage. They are not a compositional semantics. Hollow/solid does not mean Missingness/Presence, past/present, possible/actual or truth. A missing outer edge is not negation, an open sector is not an omitted Relation, a stop is not Absence, and rightward or upward placement is not improvement. The Feeds node groups are not full State glyphs; the delta is a borrowed conventional name, not a numerical restriction; sector counts do not fix the number of Transformations or States.

Exercisability's corner brackets do not resemble Permission's sheet. Admission and the Designations do not reuse CountsAs' paired record, and Role no longer shares a top bar with Authority. Constituted Sovereignty, which requires Authority (D096), still shares no element with it.
institutional_review.open_gate: Retain labels. At inline and tile sizes, check CountsAs against Recognition, Record, Tool and Price; Authority against Agent, Standing and Principal and warning-sign or tent readings; Permission Claim against Claim, Standing and Principal; Declaration against Claim, Action and send or export icons; Permission against Capability, Rule and Record; and every hollow node. Approval is a design choice, not reader-test evidence.

cross_cutting: The approved design directions in pair_review, field_review and the later dated review sections, including action_interior_review, coordination_review and institutional_review, are provisional, not semantic certification. Reader testing remains outstanding.
Arbitrary differentiators remain: dot (7 uses), foot (9, including standalone Absence), wings (3), bar (2), cap (2) and seed (1) carry no consistent meaning; the legend should say so.

Eye drawings appear in Perception, Witness, Evidential Bearing, Attestation, Intelligence and Observation, and compact eyes with hollow r=1.5 pupils in Interpretation, Agency and Embodied Perspective, importing visual seeing. Observation uses an eye inside a sheet; Evidence retains the older traced sheet. None asserts vision, consciousness, Truth or independence.

Repeated templates create near-collisions: a path crossing a vertical barrier (Sense vs Trust, and now Action's outward crossing); post-stem-box (Designations, Body; Standing and Recognition no longer use it); a box on a stem meeting an action arrow (Tool vs Respect); partial sheets with stepped paths (Reference vs Evidence); converging pairs (Attention/Care vs Enforcement); branches (Boundary Sovereignty, which keeps the former Control routing template, Substrate, Language); an eye with a fork (Interpretation vs Intelligence); a node triangle (Model's frame vs Bodily Organization's vessel, both near Configuration); sheets (Specification, Rule, Capability, Record, Observation, and Control's narrow maps-to sheet near Rule and Sign); a hollow-node zigzag (Flow vs Causal path's directed chain); a box joined to outside members or a token (Environment vs Sign); a closed record sheet with a bottom retention line (CountsAs vs Permission, both near Recognition's sheet and Record); and two full-height posts around a central figure (Standing, Principal, Authority, Permission Claim). Map's uneven mesh and Observation's enclosed eye no longer use the partial-sheet template. Consequence now ends in a delta rather than a box, so the stepped endpoint collision with CountsAs is removed, and Price no longer shares Model's linked boxes.

Staircases and arrowheads now recur across many revised glyphs (Exercisability and Constituent Power, which keep the old Capability staircase, Alignment, Care, Respect, Boundary Sovereignty, the Operative Knowledge family); Rule's and Control's maps-to and Sign's trace arrow add three more arrowheads, and action_interior_review adds arrowheads without staircases in Action, Consequence, Agency, Tool, Capability, Memory and Exposure; institutional_review adds horizontal arrowheads in Declaration and Permission, and CountsAs no longer uses a staircase or arrowhead. Ascending stairs may read as progress or improvement; upward arrows in Memory and Exposure may read as increase or upload. Causal path now uses a directed node chain, so staircase-plus-arrow no longer copies it, but any arrowhead may still suggest a completed causal path. Arrowheads are mnemonic order cues, not causal proofs.

Partial redesign leaves family breaks. Person keeps the former ring-and-axis Entity form while Entity now uses the six-sector pivot fan, so it no longer visibly shares Entity's glyph although it is an Entity; Principal now places Entity's fan between Standing's posts (coordination_review). Boundary Sovereignty keeps the old Control routing template, Body and the Designations keep the old Standing and Recognition post-stem-box template, and Knowledge Transmission keeps the old Flow wave. Constituent Exercise and Constituent Sovereignty keep gate and legs while Constituent Power keeps the old Capability staircase; Exercisability keeps it too, so neither shares the current Capability sheet. External Sovereignty keeps the old Exposure open arc and wings, while Exposure now uses the vessel. Bodily Organization and Embodied Perspective use the vessel while Body does not. Knowledge Transmission does not reuse the Operative Knowledge form. The Claim glyph is not reused by the attribution forms, CountsAs is not reused by Admission or the Designations, Admission is not reused by Evidence, the current Declaration and Permission drawings are not reused by Grant, which remains unresolved, Ledger is not reused by Price, and Polity is not reused by Constituent Power. Permission Claim and Declaration now reuse a smaller open Claim frame and Authority reuses Agent's triangle and axis (institutional_review), while Permission has left the gate that Revocation and Permission Exercise keep.

Several pairs differ only by small marks: Presence/Missingness (the central dot; Missingness is inside Presence, not its opposite); Consciousness vs Moral Attribution, and Consciousness vs Moral Designation (only a 5–6-unit tag inside the box: an angular chevron vs a curved hook); Operative/Factive/Warranted Knowledge (a small linked diamond and a corner). Observation and Evidence no longer differ merely by a small box: their visual family is broken. Set/Configuration share three dots and differ by connecting lines; State uses half-overlapping hollow/solid triangles. Invariant and Persistence differ by one spoke, and Entity extends the fan to six; Change's delta is contained whole in Agent and ActsFor. Interface is the exact Boundary plus a compact token, and Recognition is the exact Standing plus an enclosing sheet. Exposure nearly contains Interior's vessel and r=2 dot (its node sits one unit lower), adding an outward arrow, and Internal Activity Selection's selected and contrast endpoints differ only by fill. Small-size discrimination remains open.

conditionI and conditionII are arbitrary domain tags, not depictions of consciousness or morality. As drawn, conditionI is an angular right-pointing chevron, which may read as '>', 'next' or play; Agency no longer uses a sideways chevron, so that resemblance is gone. conditionII is a single curved hook, which may read as ')', a comma or a hook. Both open to the left and occupy almost the same area, so their small-size discrimination is untested.

Mnemonic, not diagram: the Absence glyph is a learned non-pictorial alias (any drawn mark is Presence, A4). Reality's filled disk is a totality cue, not a bounded model of everything; its central opening does not locate Absence within Reality.

Unwanted pictorial readings in current drawings: a therefore sign (Set), a triangular network (Configuration), two successive States or a past/present contrast (State's overlapping triangles), a mandatory greatest member or hierarchy of authority (mathematical Order's Hasse fork), a molecule or linked network (Feeds' member bridge), a progress track or slider (Causal path), control/treatment tracks (Causal Contribution's lanes), a fan, hinge or sunrise (Invariant's and Persistence's open sectors), a railway switch or choice (Constraint's selective branch), a till receipt (Receipt), linked flowchart nodes (Price), a network diagram or molecule (Model's framed node triangle, Bodily Organization's internal network), an exit or 'go' sign (Action), a warning sign or 'drop here' cue (Consequence), a split view (Interpretation's perceptual fork), 'look and go' or watching (Agency, Embodied Perspective), a lamp or hanging tag (Tool), a send button on a document (Capability), increase, upload or eject (Memory's and Exposure's upward arrows), a slingshot or choice (Internal Activity Selection), an export or sign-out icon (Operative Knowledge), chart axes (World), a file tree (Body), a figure-eight or S (Meaning), a letter F (attribution flag), an asterisk, snowflake or hub (Entity's six-sector fan), a network or tree bracket (Environment), a container or range (Scope's spans), a form or checklist (Specification), an export button (Rule), a plug or machine input (Sign), a waveform or periodic motion (Flow's zigzag), an interval, Boundary or slider (Standing), a form field or slider in a box (Recognition), an ID card or form (CountsAs' paired record), a warning sign or tent between posts (Authority), a framed portrait or goalposts (Permission Claim), a send or export icon (Declaration), and a document with an arrow (Permission). The earlier viewfinder (Configuration, State), detached minus (State), gallows, flowchart connector or plug (Standing), fluid wave (Flow), K-shaped prohibition branch (Control), ID card or toggle (Recognition), I-beam or text cursor (Principal), exchange-icon (Price), numerical comparison sign (mathematical Order), cancelled warning sign (Change), hash sign (Invariant), one-cause-two-effects fork (Causal Contribution), phi (Entity), scattered rays (Environment), list icon (Specification), minus-in-box (Rule), broken crosshair (Sign), copy/duplicate icon (Model), legs (Action), arrow-into-box download (Consequence), command-line prompt (Agency), H with hooks (Tool), level-up staircase (Capability), '=' in a cup (Memory), token-into-slot or ballot (CountsAs), command, download or enter key (Authority), psi (Declaration) and up-in-a-gate increase (Permission) readings no longer apply to the current paths.

crown remains on three sovereignty profiles (Constituent, Constituted, External) and still imports monarchy. Boundary Sovereignty no longer uses it, so the crown is not a full profile family. roots remain in Constituent Exercise and Constituent Sovereignty, importing legs or crowds; Action no longer uses them.

The vessel (U) is a learned internality cue for Interior and its five approved contents (Memory, Exposure, Bodily Organization, Embodied Perspective, Internal Activity Selection), not a universal container, a physical cavity, a Boundary drawing or consciousness. Internal Activity Selection's solid endpoint locally designates the selected alternative, not Truth, Permission, Presence or a past State; its hollow contrast is not Missingness.

Drawing clearances to check: Interface no longer uses the widened brackets and ordered path, so their earlier contacts and narrow tick gaps no longer apply. Its compact token's mitered corners sit about 0.8 unit clear of Boundary's diamond (from path coordinates), and Recognition's sheet and Principal's six hollow nodes are dense at text size, as are the hollow nodes in CountsAs, Permission Claim and Declaration and Authority's reduced triangle between posts. The earlier Boundary Sovereignty collinear stroke and the asymmetric Care arrowhead are no longer present in the current paths.
Earlier cross-catalog collisions with the Unicode study for Reality, Map, Relation and CountsAs are removed by the redesigns. Presence still matches the historical Unicode Center candidate.

entries.cue: Set's three dots joined along the two sloping sides, without a bottom edge: a Hasse-diagram mnemonic for a member Set with a partial order. Read upward, the lower pair is incomparable and each precedes the upper member; reflexive loops and transitive shortcuts are omitted.
entries.risk: May suggest exactly three members, a greatest member, mandatory branching or a hierarchy of authority. None is required: empty and total Orders remain permitted, and upward does not mean causation or improvement. The missing bottom edge can resemble an incomplete Configuration; it is not an ontological subtraction operation.
entries.recommendation: Provisional Hasse drawing approved in order_hasse_review, retaining U+E075. Use with the label Order and explain upward reading. Compare with Set, Configuration and State at text size; reader interpretation remains untested.

entries.cue: Standalone underscore: a minimal conventional name for absolute Absence, not a depiction. Its low placement concerns the inscription only; it asserts no position, ground, Boundary or Relation for Absence. Like every inscription, the mark is Presence under A4.
entries.risk: It can resemble an unfilled slot, underline, baseline or subtraction sign. An unfilled-slot reading would suggest Missingness and is not the justification for this choice. The reused foot stroke carries no consistent meaning across glyphs, and its occurrence elsewhere does not put Absence inside other terms. Its low position may be overlooked at small sizes.
entries.recommendation: Provisional underscore approved in pair_review, replacing the ring without changing the font slot. Retain its label and check tile, graph and mathematical text sizes. No dot-only exception is needed. Do not infer semantic equivalence or reader discrimination from its simplicity.

entries.cue: Unchanged ring with a central dot. Making a mark witnesses Presence under A4, but does not uniquely identify this glyph, since every inscription is Presence.
entries.risk: The ring may suggest a bounded Entity or a center in a field, neither required by A3. The circled dot also resembles solar and mathematical symbols and the historical Unicode Center candidate.
entries.recommendation: Retain the existing drawing and label. The circle is typographic, not an ontological enclosure. Design direction approved in pair_review; the underscore replacement for Absence removes the former dot-only opposition. No semantic equivalence or reader-test result is claimed.

entries.cue: Plain circle: an unfilled-field mnemonic, retaining Presence's ring without its central dot. The expected or represented item comes from A5, not from the shape alone. Missingness remains inside Presence, not absolute Absence.
entries.risk: The circle can read as zero, an empty set or an arbitrary empty container. Emptiness alone does not establish Missingness. The only visual difference from Presence is its central dot, so the pair can be confused at small sizes.
entries.recommendation: Provisional choice requested in field_review. Retain labels and check small-size discrimination from Presence; do not treat dot removal as a formal operation. This replaces frame+seed without changing the font slot or the definition.

entries.cue: Filled disk with a small clear center: an inverted-ink companion to Presence, using its circular outer contour. The filled area is a mnemonic for totality, not an exhaustive depiction of Presence.
entries.risk: The outer contour may suggest Reality is a bounded Entity; the hole may suggest Absence is a part of Reality. Neither inference is licensed. Negative space belongs to the inscription, not to absolute Absence. The opening can disappear at very small sizes, leaving a solid dot; the glyph can also resemble a washer or target.
entries.recommendation: Provisional choice requested in field_review, replacing the branching totality motif. Retain the label and check the central opening in the wall, inline math and graph. The drawing uses overlapping uniform strokes to make continuous ink; their layering carries no ontological meaning.

entries.cue: Two parallel equal-length horizontal strokes: the conventional equals sign names logical equality within Presence (D120). It matches Difference's bars before the slash. The resemblance to two underscores is a poetic association, not an ontological construction.
entries.risk: May suggest only numerical equality, similarity, or an equation-solving instruction. The two strokes do not denote two distinct beings, two Absences, or a comparison event. Reusing bars in other glyphs does not assert compositional semantics.
entries.recommendation: Use provisionally with its label; distinguish exact Identity from resemblance and preserved properties. Keep the existing geometric bars motif and append a new font slot. Verify the symbol in tiles, graph and glyph mathematics.

entries.cue: Two horizontal bars struck by a slash: a not-equals sign, now paired explicitly with Identity's equals sign. D002 negates Identity for the same compared Presences or ordered configurations.
entries.risk: Readings as numerical subtraction or inequality of magnitude. Shared bars in Ledger do not assert that it composes Identity; Memory and Bodily Organization no longer use bars.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; the Identity/Difference partition is classical, not an empirical decision procedure. The slash is a mnemonic for this pair, not a general negation operator for the alphabet.

entries.cue: Two equal horizontal bars joined by a central vertical stroke, extending slightly beyond both bars: association with distinguishable participant positions, without an arrow or staircase. The bars share Identity's proportions but do not compose its meaning.
entries.risk: Resembles the double-dagger footnote mark. The equals-like bars may suggest that Relation requires Identity, while the vertical may be mistaken for another negation stroke alongside Difference. Two bars can suggest a binary-only relation and graphic symmetry can suggest reciprocity; none is required by D003. Ordered roles are not specified by the shape alone.
entries.recommendation: Provisional design approved in relation_review. Retain the label and compare with Identity and Difference at text size. The connecting stroke names association, not equality, causation or a general operation on glyph meanings. Interface no longer uses the older ordered-path drawing; it now reuses Boundary (coordination_review). Motif reuse is not a compositional grammar.

entries.cue: Maps-to: a vertical tail bar identifies the expression side, and a horizontal stem ends in a right-facing arrowhead toward the target side. Distinct graphic roles name expression-to-target reference without a detached box or gap.
entries.risk: Mathematical maps-to notation usually describes a function and may suggest one output per input; D102 does not require a unique target for an expression across uses. The arrow may suggest causation or transformation, neither entailed. A small tail can disappear at text size, leaving a generic arrow.
entries.recommendation: Provisional design approved in denotation_review. Use the custom shared-font drawing with its label. Borrow the expression-to-target orientation, not a function's uniqueness condition; Denotation establishes neither fidelity, Truth, Interpretation, institutional status nor participation in a Causal path. Check tail visibility at text and graph sizes.

entries.cue: Three solid dots arranged at equilateral triangle vertices: membership considered without asserting further Relations among the members.
entries.risk: Resembles the mathematical therefore sign. The layout might suggest exactly three members, spatial arrangement, or that a Set excludes Relations. None follows; empty Sets and Relation members remain permitted.
entries.recommendation: Use with its label, paired with Configuration. Triangle position is typographic, not member order. Test the solid dots at inline sizes. No reader study is claimed.

entries.cue: The same three dots as Set, joined by three straight lines: members together with specified relational structure.
entries.risk: May imply every member is connected, exactly three members, participant closure, or binary-only Relations. D004 requires none of these. Ordered participant roles are not shown. Resembles a triangular network and Change's plain delta.
entries.recommendation: Use provisionally with its label. The shared dots cue the member Set; the edges cue additional structure, not an exhaustive diagram. This supersedes the earlier alias reading. State now extends the triangle family with hollow/solid half-overlap, as recorded in state_overlap_review.

entries.cue: Two equal upright Configuration-like triangles share a baseline with exactly half-base overlap: hollow vertices on the left, solid on the right. Each inner base node is at the midpoint of the other triangle's base, directly below its apex. A learned mnemonic for an indexed Configuration.
entries.risk: May suggest two successive States, a Transformation, or a past/present or possible/actual contrast. None is required; hollow vertices do not denote Missingness. The four-node baseline is crowded and hollow centers may disappear at small sizes. The drawing does not establish an index domain or its ordering.
entries.recommendation: Provisional midpoint-overlap drawing approved in state_overlap_review, retaining U+E008. Use with the State label. Compare with Configuration, Order and Change at text and graph sizes; reader interpretation remains untested.

entries.cue: Upward arrow standing on a baseline (foot): orientation away from a ground, cueing asymmetry (D006).
entries.risk: Permission no longer uses 'up' (institutional_review), so Direction is its only use, but it may still read as increase, elevation or improvement; Direction implies none of these, nor causality or chronology.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; state that vertical orientation is arbitrary and confers no valence.

entries.cue: Two equilateral triangles share the upright ghost triangle's right edge, as after a 60-degree turn. The three ghost vertices stay hollow; only the new rightmost vertex is solid, cueing input-to-output orientation without a staircase.
entries.risk: May suggest spatial rotation, rigid motion, reversibility or necessarily preserved structure and participants. None is required. Hollow/solid does not mean Missingness/Presence or possible/actual; shared vertices do not assert identity of participants. The result is intentionally not a fully solid Configuration triangle. Hollow centers may close at text size.
entries.recommendation: Option A approved in transformation_edge_review, retaining U+E00A. Keep the label; compare the shared-edge silhouette with State's half-overlap and Configuration's single triangle. The turn is a learned mnemonic, not a semantic operation or reader-test evidence.

entries.cue: Plain equilateral triangle (delta), without a slash: the conventional finite-change cue for a Difference between States joined by a Transformation (D008).
entries.risk: Delta suggests numerical difference, but D008 is not restricted to quantities. The joining Transformation is not cued. Without nodes the delta resembles Configuration's triangle, and Agent and ActsFor now contain the whole Change glyph, so they may read as kinds of Change.
entries.recommendation: Option A approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E00B. Use with the Change label; delta is a conventional name, not a numerical restriction. Compare with Configuration, Agent and ActsFor at text size; the Agent family needs a separate redesign.

entries.cue: Member bridge: two disjoint equilateral triangles of hollow nodes; one bridge joins the first triangle's right base node to the second triangle's apex. A specified part of one State supplies a specified part of another (D009).
entries.risk: Direction is weak without an arrowhead; left-to-right, downward placement is only a convention. The bridge alone does not supply the required account and does not assert equality of the joined parts. The node groups name State roles, not full State glyphs, and may read as a molecule, network or two linked Configurations. Six hollow centers and short trimmed edges may close at text size.
entries.recommendation: Option A approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E00C. Use with the Feeds label. The study geometry is scaled by 0.95 about the cell center so the outer rings stay inside the ink margin; edges stop outside hollow centers. Check the bridge and hollow centers at inline sizes.

entries.cue: Directed chain: three horizontal nodes joined in sequence, the first two hollow and the last solid, ending in a rightward arrowhead: ordered traversal sharing one orientation (D010).
entries.risk: A generic directed chain is not sufficient for a Causal path: the Transformations and Feeds joins are not shown. Hollow/solid does not mean possible/actual or past/present. It may read as a progress track, slider or playback control. Causal Contribution's lanes reuse the same row, so the two may be confused at small sizes.
entries.recommendation: Option B approved in process_preservation_review, superseding the earlier option D selection and retaining U+E00D. Use with the label; do not treat the chain as asserting the Feeds joins. Compare with Causal Contribution's lanes and generic arrows.

entries.cue: Comparison lanes: two parallel same-direction chains of three nodes with rightward arrowheads, the upper hollow throughout and the lower with solid first and last nodes. Two separately witnessed comparison paths with unlike endpoints (D103), not a fork.
entries.risk: Fill is a local contrast, not truth, actuality, Missingness or a measured effect. Matching inputs except one named Difference cannot be shown, and the downstream Change is not drawn separately. The lanes may read as two independent processes, parallel tracks or a control/treatment chart, and the lower lane resembles Causal path's chain. The upper arrowhead stops outside its hollow end node, so its tip is implied rather than drawn.
entries.recommendation: Option A approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E00E. Use with the label. It removes the fork's one-cause-two-effects and choice readings. Check the four hollow centers and the trimmed upper arrowhead at text size.

entries.cue: Two open 60-degree sectors around one filled pivot: three equal spokes end in hollow nodes, with no outer edges. A named element held while its surroundings vary under named Transformations (D011).
entries.risk: May read as a fan, hinge, compass or fixed-point rotation, suggesting pointwise or geometric invariance; D011 requires neither. The open sectors are not omitted Relations, and the filled pivot does not mean Presence or actuality. Persistence adds one sector, so the pair differs by one spoke at small sizes. Radiating spokes recall Center's wheel and the State and Transformation node graphs.
entries.recommendation: Two-sector open fan approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E00F. Use with the label; the named preserved part and Transformation family still need text. Compare with Persistence, Center and Transformation at text size.

entries.cue: Three open 60-degree sectors around one filled pivot: four equal spokes end in hollow nodes, with no outer edges. Invariant's pivot extended through one more sector: an Invariant preserved across an ordered sequence of States (D012).
entries.risk: Sector count is a drawing choice; it does not fix the number of States or show their order. The half-fan may read as a sunrise, gauge or fan. It differs from Invariant by one spoke, which may be lost at small sizes, and shares Invariant's fixed-point and Center's hub readings. Varying State Configurations are permitted but not shown.
entries.recommendation: Three open sectors (option A) approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E010; the closed-sector alternative was not adopted. Use with the label and compare with Invariant and Center at text size.

entries.cue: Selective branch: one input splits into a route that continues to a corner arrowhead and a route that meets a transverse stop. A persistent Relation excluding some Transformations while permitting others (D013).
entries.risk: The fork can imply an Agent choosing, though Constraints need no Agent; it resembles Boundary Sovereignty's routing junction (the former Control template) and the remaining fork glyphs (Intelligence, Internal Activity Selection). The stop is not Absence or Revocation. Persistence is not shown. It may read as Permission plus Revocation or as a railway switch.
entries.recommendation: Option B approved in process_preservation_review, retaining U+E011. Use with the label. It removes the earlier closeness to Rule and Scope's frame. Compare with Boundary Sovereignty and Substrate at text size.

entries.cue: Six equal 12-unit spokes from one solid pivot at the cell center, every 60 degrees, each ending in its own hollow node, with no outer hexagon: the Invariant and Persistence pivot fan carried around the full turn. A Presence reidentified across ordered States through a named Invariant and Persistence witness (D014).
entries.risk: Identity is not the six endpoints: the spokes are not six States, a complete or exhaustive history, or a causal network, and the full turn is a family resemblance, not completeness. The solid pivot does not mean Presence or actuality; hollow endpoints do not mean Missingness, and the open sectors are not omitted Relations. It may read as an asterisk, snowflake, hub or wheel, recalling Center's and Symbol's star. Principal now places this fan between Standing's posts (coordination_review). Person keeps the former ring-and-axis form, so that part of the Entity family is visibly broken; Person remains an Entity by definition (D073), not by drawing.
entries.recommendation: Six-sector open fan approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E012. Use with the label; the named Invariant, ordered States and Persistence witness still need text. Compare with Persistence, Invariant, Center and Symbol at text size. Principal's family link was repaired in coordination_review; repairing Person needs a separate review.

entries.cue: Diamond flanked by two outer vertical strokes (echo): a delimited outline set off from surroundings.
entries.risk: Reads as absolute-value/norm bars around a diamond. The diamond is shared with Symbol and Truth, so Boundary may read as truth-like or symbolic rather than D015's Constraints indexed to an identity Invariant. Echo also appears in Recurrent Integration and Constituent Power, and Boundary Sovereignty and Reference use similar outer strokes, so the outer bars have no stable Boundary meaning. Interface now contains this exact form plus a compact token (coordination_review); Sense, also defined through Boundary, does not reuse it.
entries.recommendation: Retained by Daniel's choice in identity_expression_review, superseding the tentative selective-perimeter proposal. Use with label; note that Boundary need not be geometric.

entries.cue: External set (option C): a box with a solid node, joined by an unarrowed connector to a separate bracket grouping three hollow outside members: Presence related to an Entity but not included in the identity delimited by its Boundary (D016).
entries.risk: Inclusion is not spatial: the box is not a physical container or a drawing of the Boundary, and outside placement is typographic. Three members are not required. The connector has no arrowhead and asserts no causal flow or entry. It may resemble Feeds, a network or a tree bracket; hollow members do not mean Missingness. The bracket recalls Scope's spans, and the box recalls Sign's token box.
entries.recommendation: Option C approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E014; it replaces the corner-and-dashes revision, whose surroundings stroke stays unused. Use with the label. Compare with Feeds, Scope, Sign and World at text size.

entries.cue: Square with a central dot: a framed stand-in for a point (expression position, D017).
entries.risk: Differs from Claim (gate+dot) only by the bottom edge; nothing marks non-identity with the target. Specification and Rule now use a full-height sheet and Sign a token box, so none reuses the square and dot.
entries.recommendation: Retained by Daniel's choice in identity_expression_review, superseding the tentative expression-stem proposal. Use with label; keep the square-dot form for Representation.

entries.cue: Coverage span: open upper and lower spans over three solid member dots: the set of Presences, Relations, States or Transformations to which a Representation or Constraint applies (D018).
entries.risk: Three dots force neither three members nor a nonempty Scope; empty Scopes remain possible. The spans may read as a container, a horizontal range or an ordering, though Scope need not be spatial or ordered. The dots recall Set's members, but the glyph does not compose Set with brackets. The open spans resemble Environment's bracket and generic frame corners such as Warranted Knowledge's.
entries.recommendation: Coverage span approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E016. Use with the label; the governing Representation or Constraint is not drawn. Compare with Set, Environment and Shadow system at text size.

entries.cue: Test sheet: a full-height sheet containing a condition line and a route that turns to meet a transverse result mark: a Representation that identifies a Scope and supplies a constructive decision procedure for membership or conformity (D019).
entries.risk: Constructivity cannot be inferred from the sheet: the route depicts a test, not an effective procedure, and a classical predicate drawn the same way would not thereby be a Specification. The transverse mark may read as a check, cross or Constraint's stop; it is not Absence, Revocation or rejection. The drawing is document-like and dense, with the result mark about 0.7 unit from the sheet edge. Rule shares the sheet; Representation keeps its square and dot.
entries.recommendation: Test sheet approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E017. Use with the label; the Scope and decision procedure must be supplied in prose. Compare with Rule, Map, Record, Ledger and Constraint at text size.

entries.cue: Mapping sheet: Specification's full-height sheet containing a maps-to expression (tail bar, stem and symmetric 3-unit arrowhead): a Specification of a Constraint or Transformation that maps conforming inputs to a set of outputs (D020).
entries.risk: Maps-to borrows input-to-output orientation only: a Rule need not be a function, deterministic or yield a unique output, and its output set may be plural. The arrow asserts no causation. It may read as an export, send or forward button. The inner maps-to recalls Denotation, but a Rule is not a Denotation; the shared sheet with Specification cues D020's dependency, not composition.
entries.recommendation: Mapping sheet approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E018. Use with the label; the conformity condition and output set are not drawn. Compare with Denotation, Specification and Operationalization at text size.

entries.cue: Trace into token: a hollow target node, an arrow with a symmetric 3-unit head, and a separate token box: a Representation joined to its target by a Causal path ending in the State that contains it (D021).
entries.risk: The target-to-token arrow is the causal trace direction, not Denotation's orientation, which runs from expression to target; it reverses the maps-to reading. An arrow does not confer causal status, and a merely assigned Denotation is not a trace. It may read as machine input, a plug or a download. The hollow node does not mean Missingness. Square caps make the arrow touch the node ring and box, so the glyph is one connected outline.
entries.recommendation: Trace into token approved in identity_expression_review, retaining U+E019. Use with the label and state the direction relative to Denotation. Compare with Causal path, Denotation, Environment and Knowledge Transmission at text size.

entries.cue: Diamond containing an eight-spoke asterisk (sparkle).

The Polity glyph (arch+tree+foot) is not reused. Constituent Exercise and Constituent Sovereignty keep gate and legs, so the constituent family is split visually. It keeps the old staircase's progress reading, and Capability now uses the action-specification sheet (action_interior_review), so it no longer shares the current Capability glyph.

entries.cue: Revised: an assertion flag (a post with two arms) beside a representation box containing an angular, right-pointing chevron domain tag (conditionI): a Claim asserting that a target State instantiates a separately specified candidate condition.
entries.risk: The tag is an arbitrary domain marker, not a depiction of consciousness; the chevron may read as '>', greater-than, 'next' or play. Agency no longer uses a sideways chevron (action_interior_review), so the earlier interpretive or agential resemblance is gone. The flag reads as the letter F, possibly 'false'. The Claim glyph (gate+dot) is not reused, so the link to D080's 'the Attribution is the Claim' is stipulated. It differs from Moral Status Attribution only by the small tag (angular chevron vs curved hook, both about 5–6 units) inside an 11-unit box.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the eyeball imagery (an experiencing subject, implied obtainment, against C10) and the wings-versus-cap-only distinction from Designation. Test small-size discrimination of the two tags.

entries.cue: Revised: a registration form (a post on a base line with an attached box) carrying the same conditionI chevron tag: an Order recording a consciousness status through CountsAs for an admitted Attribution.
entries.risk: The tag is arbitrary; the angular chevron may read as '>', 'next' or play. Neither the CountsAs nor the Admission glyph is reused, so the CountsAs nature (D081) is stipulated. The post-stem-box template was shared with the former Standing and Recognition drawings; Recognition now encloses the scoped placement in a sheet (coordination_review), so that resemblance no longer applies, consistent with D081's statement that Designation does not reuse Recognition. It differs from Moral Personhood Designation only by the tag, and it must not be read as altering Standing or Personhood.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the eyeball imagery and the cap-versus-wings-only distinction. Consider sharing a visible element of CountsAs.

entries.cue: Square pierced by an arrow, with a small seed below: a representation entering a causal path (D082).
entries.risk: Seed is arbitrary; discriminating selection and Interface are not shown. The seed is now unique to this glyph, and its square+arrow resembles revised Operative Knowledge's box-with-outgoing-arrow.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; state the seed is arbitrary.

entries.cue: Revised: an L-shaped scope corner enclosing a stepped figure with posts: a scoped Configuration of Entities and available paths.
entries.risk: It may read as chart axes with a step-function plot, or as a building or skyline. Entities, the selected Presence of their Environments, the available Causal paths and the common Invariant (D083) are not distinguished. Environment no longer uses an L corner, so the earlier shared cue is gone.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the planet imagery and the orbit shared with Environment. Test against chart readings.

entries.cue: Revised: four parallel source lines joined into one feed that splits into two outputs (one diagonal, one stepped): a persistent source of input States for a family of Transformations.
entries.risk: The comb may read as a bus, a plug, a hamburger menu or the letter E, and the split as a fork or choice resembling Boundary Sovereignty's routing (the former Control template). The Substrate's own Constraints shaping outputs (D084) are not cued separately, and contextuality is not visible.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the passive-container vessel and the ties to Interior and Body.

entries.cue: Diamond on a full vertical axis with a dot on the axis: a plumb/aligned gem, plausibly 'representation aligned with what is'.
entries.risk: CountsAs and Price no longer use the diamond, so the institutional tie is gone; the diamond remains shared with Boundary and Symbol, and the gem reading implies value. Dot sits on the axis stroke. Factive and Warranted Knowledge deliberately echo it with a small diamond on an axis.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; keep the diamond+axis link reserved for Truth-involving terms.

entries.cue: Revised: a source post on the left and a path through an opening in a vertical barrier, ending in an arrowhead: a contribution from one Entity passing another Entity's admitting Constraint.
entries.risk: Which side trusts is ambiguous: the arrow points away from the post, so it may read as the post's outgoing action rather than an admitted contribution. Insufficient Control and the Causal Contribution (D086) are not cued. The template is nearly the same as Sense's.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the symmetric link and the near-identity of Relation plus foot. Differentiate it from Sense and make the trusting side clear.

entries.cue: Revised: an ascending stepped subject path meeting a target corner post with a reference tick: an ordered subject conforming to a target under a correspondence Specification.
entries.risk: The ascending steps may read as progress or improvement, against D087's rejection of Alignment as a global virtue. The diagonal join to the target may read as merging with, or identity with, the target. The correspondence Specification is not legible.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the Persistence rails and the symmetry: roles are now ordered. Consider a non-ascending subject path.

entries.cue: Eye with a fork: perception branching into adapted choices.
entries.risk: Eye implies visual or perceptual intelligence; model construction across non-enumerated states (D088) is not cued.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.cue: Revised as a linked family member: a record box with an inner mark and an arrow issuing from inside the box to the right, a Record discriminatingly conditioning a path to action.
entries.risk: A box with an outgoing arrow is the common 'export/sign out' icon, which may suggest that knowledge leaves the record (transmission) rather than conditioning an interpreter's action. The capable interpreter and the Specification (D089) are not shown. Knowledge Transmission (square+wave+arrow) does not reuse this form.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the eye/preview-icon reading and gives Factive and Warranted Knowledge a visibly shared base.

entries.cue: Square, wave and arrow: a record carried across to a recipient.
entries.risk: The wave is the former Flow drawing; Flow now uses an open node sequence (coordination_review), so the wave no longer links it to Flow, though it may still suggest recurrence or signal transmission; D090 preserves operative function, not record identity. Operative Knowledge now uses a box-with-inner-path form that this glyph does not share, although D090 relates two Operative Knowledge instances.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; consider aligning with the revised Operative Knowledge form.

entries.cue: Revised: Operative Knowledge plus a small diamond on an axis at upper right, echoing the Truth glyph (diamond, axis), joined by a short link stroke to the record box's right edge: Truth obtains for the carried Claim.
entries.risk: The link ties the truth mark to the record rather than to the action arrow, which reduces the earlier risk of reading the Action or Consequence as true, but the diamond still sits above the arrowhead and its link may read as a tag, key or balloon string; whether readers attach it to the record's carried Claim (D091) is untested. The diamond may read as a gem or a kite.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the near-invisible seed: the differentiator is now visible, linked to Truth and linked to the record. Test that the mark is read as qualifying the record, not the action.

entries.cue: Revised as a linked family member: the Factive form plus a corner bracket at lower right, Factive Operative Knowledge with admitted supportive Evidence.
entries.risk: The warrant bracket is generic (it reads as Scope or a frame corner) and does not reuse the Evidence form, so admitted Evidence, the independent Witness and supportive bearing (D092) are stipulated. At x=30 it sits about 2 units clear of the arrowhead tip (x=27), which may crowd at small sizes.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the previous omission: it now visibly keeps both the Operative and Factive forms (C20). Consider an Evidence-family marker instead of a generic corner.

entries.cue: Revised: the assertion flag and representation box carrying a single curved hook domain tag (conditionII): a Claim asserting a candidate moral condition.
entries.risk: The tag is an arbitrary domain marker, not a depiction of morality; the hook may read as ')', a comma, an apostrophe or a fishhook. Only the inner tag distinguishes it from Consciousness Attribution, and the curved hook and angular chevron occupy almost the same area, so small-size discrimination is untested. It shares the F-flag reading and the missing Claim-glyph link. It must not be read as establishing the condition (D093).
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the Eye-of-Providence imagery and the collision with Meaning.

entries.cue: Revised: the registration form carrying the conditionII curved hook tag: an Order recording moral-personhood status for an admitted Moral Status Attribution.
entries.risk: The tag is arbitrary; the hook may read as ')' or a comma. Only the tag distinguishes it from Consciousness Designation, and CountsAs is not reused. It must not be read as institutional Person or as the candidate condition (D094).
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the contained Person stick figure: no Person form remains.

entries.cue: Square gate with crown and legs: a plural body realizing founding power over an Order.
entries.risk: Crown imports monarchy; legs import a crowd. The crown is now limited to three sovereignty profiles, but this glyph does not reuse the revised Constituent Power form, which D095 requires.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label; consider aligning with Constituent Power and dropping the legs.

entries.cue: Square gate with crown on a baseline: maximal authority within an Order.
entries.risk: No longer near-identical to Authority, which was redrawn, but it now shares no element with Authority although D096 requires Standing and Authority. Crown suggests universal supremacy, while D096 maximality is relative.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.cue: Revised: two outer posts (a Boundary) enclosing the former Control routing mark, with a source line splitting into a blocked (crossed) upper branch and an admitted lower branch that ends in a right-angled arrowhead.

The arrowhead is a mnemonic, not a causal proof. Order Enforcement is not shown (the Enforcement glyph is not reused) and the witnessed Difference in Consequence is not legible. Without the crown, the sovereignty profiles no longer share a family cue, which is acceptable since they do not entail one another (D095–D098).

Its visible link to Control was to the former routing drawing; Control now uses the adjusted rule (coordination_review), so that link is broken. Test that the lower arrowhead reads as admission, not outflow.

entries.cue: Open arc with crown and wings: sovereign status recognized from outside.
entries.risk: Built on the old Exposure drawing (open+wings), which may still imply an exposed interior; D098 records external Standing, not Control or Exposure. Exposure now uses the vessel and an outward arrow (action_interior_review), not cascaded here, so the shared form is broken.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.risk: Renders like a down arrow, although no current glyph uses the down arrow; may read as directional causation rather than D099's asymmetric ordering.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.cue: Staircase between rails on a baseline: a graduated scale.
entries.risk: Implies a numerical ladder that represents preference; D100 requires a separate correspondence witness.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.cue: Revised: a closed record square containing two small, slightly unequal consideration slots (upper left and lower right) joined by a stepped connector: a recorded exchange condition relating two considerations.

Linked boxes may now read as a flowchart, network or 'linked items' icon. Model now uses an organized node surface (action_interior_review), so Price no longer shares its linked boxes. Nothing marks which slot is offered or required. The Ledger glyph (square+rails+bars) and CountsAs are not reused.

entries.risk: Shares double with Recurrent Integration and now Meaning (which derives from it, appropriately); no link to Flow or Memory (D105).
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

Without the axis it is as close to Recurrent Integration (double+bar+echo) as to Ritual. Participant indices are stipulated.

Interior, Boundary and the identity Invariant are not cued, and the post-stem-box element resembles the Designations; Standing and Recognition no longer use it (coordination_review). Bodily Organization and Embodied Perspective still use the vessel and do not share this form.

The triangle shows mutual connection, not at least two Organs, their recurring Transformations, Causal Contributions or the required inter-Organ feed under a shared Direction, and three nodes do not require three Organs. It nearly repeats Model's framed triangle and resembles Configuration and a molecule. It no longer contains Memory's bars or shares Declaration's tree, and it still shares no form with the revised Body glyph.

The condition Representation, the advertised internal Transformations and the Causal Contributions are not legible. The compact eye recalls Interpretation and Agency, and the vessel does not link to the revised Body glyph under whose Body Relation D109 is scoped. The former axis is gone.
entries.recommendation: Option B approved in action_interior_review, retaining its slot. Keep the label; compare with Perception, Interpretation and Agency at inline sizes.

entries.risk: Shares double with Ritual and Meaning; echo shared with Boundary and Constituent Power.
entries.recommendation: Retain with label.

entries.cue: Emphasized alternative (Internal Activity Selection C): the unchanged vessel contour holding an open equilateral 60-degree sector, a lower hollow node branching to two upper endpoints, the upper-left solid and the upper-right hollow: one determination among at least two available Transformations within the Interior (D111).

The branch may read as choice and import Agency, though D111 states it 'does not by itself constitute Action or Agency'. The outcome and contrast Representations and the Causal Contribution are not legible. The open sector recalls Invariant's pivot fan, an inverted Mathematical Order Hasse fork and Bodily Organization's triangle without its top edge; the two endpoints differ only by fill at small sizes.
entries.recommendation: Option C approved in action_interior_review, retaining its slot. Keep the label; compare with Bodily Organization, Invariant, Mathematical Order and Constraint at inline sizes.

entries.cue: Revised as a linked family member: two stepped lines converging into a parallel pair aimed at a vertical target bar, Perception or Interpretation organized by a target.
entries.risk: The narrowing may read as a funnel or plug, suggesting a finite channel or degree that D114 does not require. The target is static, so organization across changes in the target's State is not shown. It resembles Enforcement's converging pair and bar.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the eye (visual only) and the up arrow (increase), and gives Care a base. Separate it from Enforcement.

entries.cue: Revised: the Attention form with an action path branching down from its lower line's riser and running right beneath it to a symmetric arrowhead inset from the right edge: Attention conditioning the selection or adjustment of Action.

The arrowhead is now symmetric (45° wings), but its lower wing ends at y=30, close to the bottom margin, and the action path (y=26) continues one unit below the first segment of Attention's lower line (y=25), a tight jog at small sizes. It shares Attention's resemblance to Enforcement. The arrow is a mnemonic order cue, not a causal proof.
entries.recommendation: Revised trial awaiting review. It addresses the nurturing/benevolence imagery (care may be incompetent, unwanted or harmful), the missing Attention link and the earlier asymmetric arrowhead. Test small-size legibility of the lower jog.

entries.risk: The crossing may read as a plus sign, checkpoint or barrier, suggesting prohibition, though the arrow passes through. The box on a line may read as a flag or key. The acting Entity is not shown, and expressed conditions are not distinguished from contextual ones.
